text:
erin: FYI — ACME (tenant: acme-prod) reported rerank calls started returning model errors after last night's deploy. Customer saw: `400` with body 'model_id not found' and lots of zero scores. Started ~11:02 UTC.

support-bot: Automated alert: 5xx/4xx spike on /v1/rerank for tenant acme-prod between 11:02-11:05 UTC (count=18). Logged request_ids included.

jason: Can you paste an example request/response from the customer? Need the exact model id they used.

erin: Pasting sanitized payload from their support ticket: ```curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"rerank-2023-large-v2","query":"Which FAQ is about billing?","documents":[{"id":"d1","text":"Billing and invoices"},{"id":"d2","text":"Pricing tiers"}]}'
```

response: ```{ "error": { "message": "model 'rerank-2023-large-v2' not found", "type": "invalid_request_error", "code": "model_not_found" }, "request_id":"req_abc123" }```

mike-oncall: That model name looks deprecated — I think we rotated alias rerank-2023-* to rerank-2024-* last quarter. Could be an alias mapping issue (alias still resolving for some tenants).

eng-runtime: Jumping in — can you confirm whether the tenant was on dedicated routing or hosted? If dedicated, alias snapshot syncing could be out-of-date.

erin: Hosted API (not Dedicated). Customer is low-volume but heavy on rerank calls.

sanjay: I pulled routing logs for req_abc123: backend returned 404 from model-registry service: `alias_lookup: no active model for alias 'rerank-2023-large-v2'`. However our alias-migration job shows an incomplete split: ~12 tenants still have legacy alias bindings.

jason: Ok — repro steps for eng: 1) Use tenant acme-prod creds 2) POST above payload to /v1/rerank 3) observe 400 model_not_found. I can provide logs and request ids offline.

eng-runtime: Investigation notes: the alias-migration job had a transient DB lock during last deploy which caused partial commit. For hosted tenants, we fallback to returning model_not_found rather than silently mapping to a compatible variant — that behavior is intended to avoid quality surprises.

mike-oncall: Customer impact: some rerank responses are zeros and some calls are flat 400. They're escalating to Sales. We should patch quickly.

eng-runtime: Short-term mitigation: re-run alias-sync for affected tenant IDs (we can force rebind alias -> new-model-id). I'll run a targeted sync for acme-prod and 11 other tenants now.

support-bot: Action logged: #SR-4821 created, priority=P1, owner=eng-runtime.

erin: Thanks — please post update here when done so I can reply to the customer with repro and mitigation steps.

eng-runtime: Done — rebind completed at 11:12 UTC for acme-prod. Post-fix verification: rerank call now returns 200 with scores. Example response: ```{ "scores":[0.87,0.12], "request_id":"req_def456" }```

mike-oncall: Confirmed with customer on reply thread — they validated scoring looks normal. Customer asked for root cause; will they need an SLA credit?

eng-runtime: Root cause = partial alias-migration commit due to DB lock during deploy. Remediation = re-run alias-sync and add retry/transaction to migration job. Filed infra ticket for durable migration (infra#1298).

jason: Marking resolved from support side after customer ack. Follow-ups: 1) schedule migration-job hardening 2) add monitoring alert when alias-sync leaves >0 tenants unbound.

erin: Great, closing here. :white_check_mark: If anything else pops up, ping me.
